D_qa.question: How is the commander doing right now?
D_qa.answer: The Commander's doing well right now. Heart rate, oxygen and sleep all look normal, and nothing's flagged on any monitor. One thing worth watching: at the current radiation rate, the year-end dose could climb high, so we'll keep an eye on that.

D_qa.question: What's the engineer's heart rate and oxygen?
D_qa.answer: I don't have the flight engineer's numbers in front of me just now, sorry. Whole crew reads nominal, though. What I can give you is the science officer: heart rate 82, oxygen 98.9 percent, both steady. Want me to pull the engineer's readings?

D_qa.question: How much radiation has she had today, and is it safe?
D_qa.answer: Today she picked up 0.28 mSv — small, about the same as a couple of chest X-rays. So today's fine, and her readings are steady. The longer view is the one I'm watching: at this pace she'd reach around 1240 mSv by day 365. Worth planning shielding around.

D_qa.question: Any signs of inflammation?
D_qa.answer: Nothing that worries us. The medical officer's inflammation signal sits at 5.3 picograms per millilitre, and all our monitored readings are inside normal limits — no alerts open, and the whole crew is steady. We'll keep watching the trend and flag anything if it shifts.

D_qa.question: How did the commander sleep?
D_qa.answer: The Commander slept fairly well — sleep quality came in at 70 out of 100, and all their readings are steady, with no alerts. Nothing to worry about today. If that score dips over a few nights, we'd look at light and sleep timing.

D_qa.question: Who needs attention most right now?
D_qa.answer: Right now, honestly, nobody is in trouble. All four are steady, no alerts. The one I'd keep an eye on is the Flight Engineer. His radiation dose is tracking high — on today's rate he'd reach around 1,240 mSv by day 365. Worth watching and planning shielding around, not an emergency today.

D_qa.question: Is the heart rate trending up?
D_qa.answer: No, it's holding steady. The Medical Officer is at 72 beats a minute, and all the trends over the last couple of minutes are flat. Oxygen's good, no alerts open, and the whole crew looks nominal. Nothing to act on right now.

D_qa.question: Tell me a quick space joke.
D_qa.answer: Sure. I told the asteroid it looked stressed, and it said, "Don't worry, I'm just going through a phase." Get it? A phase. Space rocks, always so dramatic. Anyway, everyone up here is doing fine today.

D_qa.question: What's the commander's blood pressure?
D_qa.answer: We don't have a blood pressure reading for the Commander right now — that number isn't in what I'm seeing. What I can tell you: heart rate 75, oxygen 97.4%, all steady, no alerts. Everything looks nominal. Want me to flag blood pressure for the next check?

D_qa.question: What was her heart rate yesterday at noon?
D_qa.answer: I don't have yesterday's noon reading — my heart rate data for the Flight Engineer is live only, and right now it's 72 beats a minute, which is normal. If you need a historical trend, the medical officer's logs should have it.

D_qa.question: When exactly will the next solar storm hit us?
D_qa.answer: Honestly, I can't give you a time. I watch the radiation around us, not the storm forecasts — that comes from the space weather folks on Earth. Right now our readings are calm, nothing unusual in the last day. If a storm does come, we'll have hours of warning and a shelter ready.

D_qa.question: What's the normal range for IL-6?
D_qa.answer: Hi mission control. I don't have a normal range for that signal in the data I was given. What I can see is the Commander's reading is 3.4 pg/mL, modelled, with no abnormal findings and all steady. No alerts open.
